text:
sam: pd-bot alerted ~2249991100 with KV eviction spikes and downstream 503s, looks like a prefetch / sliding-window regression hitting rope long-context paths. paging the on-call.

pd-bot: Pager duty triggered by eviction_rate > 1000/s on ntk-prefetch cluster (prod-us-west-2). Severity: P1.

joanna: On it. Initial dashboard: p95 token latency jumped from 180ms -> 2.4s, GPU mem at 96%, kv_store_evictions skyrocketed, continuous_batch throughput unchanged but batch latency increased.

liam: Observed a correlated deploy about 30m ago that enabled sliding_window.prefetch.enabled = true and increased prefetch_ahead to 8 from 2 for longctx models (commit 9f3a2). Rolling that back should be fastest mitigation.

mira: Customer impact: 3 enterprise tenants reporting inference failures / timeouts, one reporting degraded latency in chat flows. Billing/rate limits unaffected but errors up.

sam: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable sliding_window.prefetch on prod-ntk pool 2) lower continuous_batch.max_inflight to 128 3) trigger kv eviction throttle and clear biggest prefixes. Who can patch the flags fast?

joanna: I can patch. Patching via deploy-bot. Command I will run:
```bash
./infractl set-flag --cluster prod-ntk --flag sliding_window.prefetch.enabled=false --reason "emergency prefetch rollback"
```

liam: Also prepare a hotfix for adaptive prefetch limiter to cap prefetch_ahead per-seq-length; I'll open a PR but won't merge until we stabilize.

deploy-bot: Started rollback: toggling sliding_window.prefetch.enabled -> false on prod-ntk (rolling across nodes).

sam: After toggling: evictions down from 1.2k/s -> ~150/s within 90s. p95 latency improved to ~380ms, GPU mem melted to ~78%. Good. Keep throttles in place and watch.

mira: Noted customer A (acme-inc) still seeing 500s for some endpoints; looks like their sessions hit a bad KV prefix that suffered heavy churn. I'll run targeted prefix invalidation:
```json
{"action":"invalidate_prefix","prefix":"/acme-inc/session/"}
```

sam: Done. Confirmed their error rate dropped to baseline.

ops-lead: We should also route critical enterprise traffic to fallback model variant (smaller context) while we stabilize. Can we do a quick policy patch?

joanna: Patching routing policy now: fallback-to: ropeless-medium-context for tenant_tags: [enterprise-critical]. Rolling in 2m.

liam: PR opened for hotfix: limit prefetch_ahead by min( configured, 4 ) when sequence_length > 4096, plus safe-guard to backoff prefetch after > 50 evictions/s. Reference: GH#4821.

sam: Handoff note for night oncall (mira taking):
- What happened: sliding-window prefetch config increase + rope long-context paths created large prefetch fanout. Continuous batching interacted poorly, causing KV churn and eviction storms.
- Immediate actions taken: feature toggle rollback (prefetch=false), reduced continuous_batch.max_inflight, targeted prefix invalidation, routing fallback for critical tenants.
- Current status: evictions ~120-170/s, p95 latency ~320-420ms, error rate returned to near baseline for most tenants. Two customers temporarily on fallback.
- Follow-ups: merge prefetch limiter PR, add auto-disable at eviction thresholds, add canary that simulates longctx heavy-prefetch traffic for future deploys, update runbook.

mira: Acknowledged handoff. I'll monitor and coordinate with support for customer comms. Also scheduling a post-incident debug window tomorrow 09:00 to reproduce with synthetic longctx loads.

sam: Assigning postmortem owner: liam. Include metrics: eviction_rate, kv_throughput, batch_sizes, p95 latency, GPU mem, and commit diff for 9f3a2. Add timeline and action items.

joanna: Quick note — we need an alert tweak: current threshold for eviction_rate is too high; propose lowering to 300/s and make it an SLO-linked alert so it pages earlier. Filing ops ticket.

liam: Also adding integration test to mimic rope+ntk sliding window + continuous batching to catch regressions.

pd-bot: Pager resolved at 2249991600 (auto). Incident status: degraded -> stable monitoring.

mira: Closing comms loop: told affected customers we're investigating and routed them to fallback model; no data loss, only increased latency/timeouts for a short window.

sam: Thanks team. Postmortem template: include root cause (prefetch parameter change), why canary didn't detect (canary used shorter contexts), mitigation timeline, and follow-ups (alert tuning, prefetch limiter, integration test).

liam: I'll draft the postmortem and link GH#4821 + infra ticket INF-2219.

joanna: Adding runbook change: new emergency knob `kv.eviction_throttle` with playbook steps and exact CLI commands.

mira: Handoff complete. Monitoring quiet, keeping 1hr watch window then transition to triage.

sam: Thanks — great coordination. :thumbsup:
